steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Interest rates set by the Bank of England affect borrowing costs: higher rates = more expensive loans and mortgages, reducing consumer spending and business investment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time: high inflation erodes purchasing power and increases business costs, but low stable inflation (2% target) indicates a healthy economy.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Exchange rates affect import/export prices: a stronger pound makes imports cheaper but exports more expensive, hurting UK exporters but helping importers.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The business cycle has four stages: boom (high growth, low unemployment), recession (negative growth, rising unemployment), recovery (growth returns), and slowdown.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how a rise in interest rates from 2% to 5% might affect a business that has a large bank loan. | Analyse how a strengthening of the pound against the euro would affect a UK business that exports to France. | Evaluate whether a recession is always bad for businesses.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link economic changes to specific business effects - don't just define terms, show the chain of impact. When discussing exchange rates, specify which direction helps/harms importers vs exporters. Remember: the same economic change can be positive for some businesses and negative for others.
